tagline: Through old Englewood and over the Myakka on SR 776.
intro: SR 776 leaves US 41 near Venice and runs southwest into Englewood, then turns east past Rotonda West, crosses the Myakka River into El Jobean and ends back on US 41 at Murdock. It is the spine of a 47-mile byway.

Through Englewood, Dearborn Street and River Road carried an early route of the Tamiami Trail until the trail was moved further north by the 1930s. East of El Jobean the road was widened onto the bed of the Charlotte Harbor and Northern Railway, abandoned in 1981, and the Cape Haze Pioneer Trail now follows more of that railroad south from SR 776.

moments.title: Englewood
moments.text: Three brothers from Englewood, Chicago platted the town in 1896 and named its streets after home, Dearborn among them, and after the freezes of the 1890s fish became its chief product.

moments.title: Manasota Key
moments.text: Beach Road crosses Lemon Bay to an 11-mile key named for a lumber company whose name joined manatee and Sarasota.

moments.title: El Jobean
moments.text: Across the Myakka sits a town laid out in the 1920s by Joel Bean, who made its name by shuffling the letters of his own.
